description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/sub.t's inline
`ok(1,'SKIP')` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING, SILENT, and general.

REPRO (scratch/p12-undef-glob-full.pl in the s464ay worktree):

    our $s = 5; our @a = (9); our %h = (k=>1);
    sub c { "code" }
    undef *s; undef *a; undef *h; undef *c;
    print "scalar: ", (defined $s ? "STILL $s" : "cleared"), "\n";
    print "array:  ", (@a ? "STILL @a" : "cleared"), "\n";
    print "hash:   ", (%h ? "STILL ".join(",",%h) : "cleared"), "\n";
    print "code:   ", (defined &c ? "STILL ".c() : "cleared"), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  cleared / cleared / cleared / cleared
  PCL:          STILL 5 / STILL 9 / STILL k,1 / STILL code

Nothing is printed on stderr: the statement is lowered and executed, it just
does nothing.  That is the #964 failure mode -- a plausible answer that is
silently the OLD one -- and it is the reason it survived: the only row that
tests it had been replaced by an inline SKIP.

WHICH ROW IT OWNS: perl-tests/sub.t row 24 `goto &xsub when @_ does not exist`
(`undef *_; eval { &utf8::encode }; is *_{ARRAY}, undef`).  PCL answers
'ARRAY(0xb)'.  Restored to the upstream assertion in s464ay and DELIBERATELY
NOT registered as a skip -- it is a fix target; the row is in
baselines/fail-baseline.tsv with this task as its cause.  The same row exists
in the companion suite (t/op/sub.t) inside its blessed count.

THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS IT HID BEHIND: the inline skip said "PCL implements
*_{ARRAY} syntax (returns \@_), but cannot 'undef *_' to make @_ undefined,
and &utf8::encode is not a PCL built-in".  Half right by accident and
mis-scoped: it reads as a quirk of `*_`, so nobody noticed that `undef *name`
does nothing for ANY glob.  `utf8::encode` IS available (it is a ruled no-op,
not-supported.md 'Unicode semantics differences') and is not what fails here.

RELATION TO #602 (done): `*A = *B` used to leave the slots B lacks untouched;
#602 made glob COPY clear them (probed still correct here: `*z =
*neverdefinedglob` clears $z).  `undef *GLOB` is the same family and was not
covered -- the clearing primitive #602 added is presumably the one `undef` on
a glob should call.

FIX SHAPE (untried, sized from #602's note): route `undef` on a GLOB operand
to #602's clear-every-slot path -- scalar -> a fresh undef box, array -> empty
vector, hash -> empty table, code -> fmakunbound.  Check first whether `undef
*x` even reaches a glob-aware arm of p-undef or is silently discarded; the
absence of any stderr says a missing-case is being swallowed somewhere, which
is also a CLAUDE.md rule-12 question (a missing case must DIE, not fall
through).

RELATED, NOT THE SAME: docs/not-supported.md 'Live symbol-table hashes'
([DEFERRED]) says "scalar/array/hash/IO glob slots are absent" -- that is
about the STASH view (%Foo::), not about `undef` on a glob whose slots PCL
does represent (it prints them fine).  Do not close this by pointing at that
entry.
=== DONE (s470bi) ===
ROOT CAUSE, exactly as filed -- a silent no-op, and the diagnosis names two
mismatched contracts: `p-undef`'s glob arm called
`(p-glob-undef-name (package-name (p-typeglob-package val)) â¦)` -- the **CL**
spelling, "MAIN" -- and the callee wanted PERL spellings: it did
`(find-package (%pcl-invert-case "MAIN"))` = `(find-package "main")` = NIL,
and its `(when pkg â¦)` swallowed the entire body.

TWO MORE DEFECTS BEHIND IT, so fixing the lookup alone would have left `undef`
half-done: the CODE slot's `fmakunbound` never removed the *p-declared-subs*
entry (`defined &c` and `exists &c` stayed true -- perl answers 0 to both), and
the IO slot was not touched at all (perl's `undef *FH` makes `*FH{IO}` undef
and a later `print FH` return undef with $! = Bad file descriptor).

FIX = ONE READING (rule 11).  `undef *G` and the clear half of `*A = *B` ask
the same question and #602 had already answered it for the copy path, so the
three clear halves come OUT of the `%p-glob-copy-*-slot` helpers as
`%p-glob-clear-{var,code,io}-slot` and both spellings call them.  They take the
PACKAGE OBJECT and the ALREADY-INVERTED name -- `%p-glob-syms-in`'s pair, the
one a p-typeglob carries -- so nothing is re-derived from strings, which is
what the bug was.  `p-glob-undef-name` is renamed `p-glob-undef` (one caller;
nothing emits it).

The aggregate slots go through `%p-glob-empty-slot`, NOT makunbound: makunbound
was tried and measured -- it gives perl's `*a{ARRAY}` answer AND `push @a, 42`
still re-vivifies, but a plain READ then CRASHES on the unbound symbol-macro
cell.  Filed as **#1117**, which also inherits `perl-tests/sub.t` row 24's
cause (re-pointed by hand in `baselines/fail-baseline.tsv` and the
`baselines/pass-baseline.tsv` header note).

MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470bi/p1020/, default AND PCL_OPT=none):
the four-slot reproducer, `exists &c` / `exists &d` after undef of a defined
and of a FORWARD-declared sub, `undef *FH` + `print FH` + `*FH{IO}`, the
slot-introspection ORDER (a read RE-VIVIFIES the ARRAY slot in perl too --
probing it in the wrong order is what made this look like agreement once),
`*A = *B` still copying and clearing, and `undef *nosuchthing` creating
nothing.  Every VALUE spelling is byte-identical to perl.

GUARD `Pl/t/glob-undef-01.t` (5 rows, 1 s): three for the fix, two INVERSES for
the copy path the helpers were extracted from.  Inverse-verified against main
(rows 1-3 fail there, 4-5 pass on both); every expectation is perl's own
output, extracted from the file and run.

Runtime-only, so corpus-diff cannot see it -- the sweep is owed (Fable).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `undef *GLOB` is a NO-OP -- perl empties all four slots ($x, @x, %x, &x), PCL leaves every one of them untouched and says nothing
